messages:
maria: heads up — the strict fncall validation we rolled out to the eu-west slice is spiking rejects. seeing ~6% reject rate for that slice vs ~0.4% baseline. not confident this is purely input drift. 

josh: can you paste the top reject examples and a link to the chart? which metric exactly spiked (rejects vs fallback vs degen route)? :eyes:

maria: chart: https://console.redwood.internal/d/validators/euwest?panel=fncall_rejects (slice=canary-eu). spike is rejects (validator.rejects) and a correlated increase in fallback->degen_count. snippet of a typical rejected response: 
```json
{"tool_response": ["ok","done"], "validation_error": "expected object for tool_response, got array"}
```

kevin: that payload explains it — some upstream adapters are returning arrays instead of the object shape. are rejects being attributed to the original route or to the fallback route in telemetry? we need clarity for billing and rollout decisions.

sara: from console traces I see the route_id maps to the original model route but the post-validate router re-assigned route_tags to degen. the dashboard panels currently show only final route_tag for cost attribution which is confusing. customers see charges on the original route but console highlights the degen path.

rollout-bot: Canary 'strict-validate-v2' in eu-west: automatic pause triggered (reject_rate > 2.5% for 3/5 mins) — paused by system.

maria: thanks bot. immediate ask: we need two quick changes before unpausing — (1) surface reject_reason histograms and a link to sampled traces in the rollout panel, (2) make it explicit whether rejects are counted as billable tokens/requests in the rollout UI and billing dashboard. both will cut the back-and-forth with CS and PM.

josh: agree. implementation notes: we currently emit `validator.code` in the logs but the UI expects a human label; also sampling for traces is only at 1/100 for rejects. propose bumping sampling to 1/10 for canary slices for next 2 hours.

kevin: on the infra side I can add a normalizer that maps common adapter shapes to a stable `reject_reason` (e.g. `TOOL_SHAPE_ARRAY_INSTEAD_OF_OBJ`) so the histogram is meaningful. will add a feature flag so we can roll it out quickly. also will expose header `X-Validate-Sample: 1` to force a trace sample from the SDK.

sara: also need a small UX tweak: in rollout detail show two counters side-by-side: `rejects (original route)` and `rejects (post-validate fallback)`. it will stop us guessing if it's a validator vs routing bug.

maria: I'll file the platform ticket and add acceptance criteria. PLAT-3321 created: "euwest strict-validate pause follow-up: reject_reason histogram + sample traces + billing attribution flag". assigning to @josh and @kevin.

josh: picking this up — i'll prototype the histogram and the sample link this afternoon. will use existing diag-panel component so low-risk.

kevin: i'll wire the normalizer and the sampling header. plan to flip feature flag to beta and test on canary slice.

sara: saved a few sample traces to the ticket for QA. also cc'ing @support to prep customer comms if we unpause and see residual rejects.

maria: sweet. TL;DR: dont unpause until we have the histogram + trace link + billing attribution clarified. quick sync in 15m in #eng-platform if you can. :thumbsup:
